mother-infant calls
Communication

Harmonic uuh' calls specific to this population, produced by mothers to retrieve separated infants and which differ from mother-infant calls in other orangutan populations

Vertical: UnknownHorizontal: UnknownOblique: Unknown

Description: Harmonic uuh' calls specific to this population, produced by mothers to retrieve separated infants and which differ from mother-infant calls in other orangutan populations

Vertical: Specific modes unclear, "the results presented here strongly suggest that these sounds were invented in each population and subsequently spread through social learning" (Wich et al. 2012)

Neesia tool use
Foraging

Orangutans using stick tools to extract seeds from Neesia fruits

Vertical: UnknownHorizontal: UnclearOblique: Unknown
Evidence and details

Description: Orangutans using stick tools to extract seeds from Neesia fruits

Vertical: suspected unknown

Horizontal: Suaq orangutans "are also the most gregarious and socially tolerant among the known study populations (van Schaik, 1999; van Schaik et al., 1999). Likewise, the two other swamps with known Neesia tool use have high densities, and therefore probably above-average gregariousness and social tolerance. Hence, suitable transmission conditions are probably the critical factor to explain the geographic distribution of skills such as feeding tool use in orangutans" (van Schaik & Knott 2001)

Oblique: suspected unknown

Domains: foraging

nesting calls
Communication

Orangutans sometimes produce a call after building their nightly nest. Calls vary among populations. In Suaq, this is described a

Vertical: UnknownHorizontal: UnknownOblique: Unknown
Evidence and details

Description: Orangutans sometimes produce a call after building their nightly nest. Calls vary among populations. In Suaq, this is described a "raspberry" call, differing from calls/lack thereof at other sites (Wich et al. 2012)

Vertical: Inferred vocal learning due to innovation of unique calls and experiments on great apes showing social learning, but unclear from research thus far.

Domains: communication

Social unit: Individual. "The high spatial overlap of the individuals in this swamp population of orangutans shows that spatially discrete social units do not exist. However, there is evidence for non-random association among females and between females and males, and hence some form of socially distinct social units...the 'community' can be considered to consist of one or more female clusters and the adult male they all prefer as mate, who has a more limited home range than those of the other males found in the area. However, it is important to point out that this ëcommunityí is not nearly as discrete as that of other fission-fusion primate species, showing neither spatial nor social exclusivity" (Singleton & van Schaik 2001) [4]

Conservation status: Critically Endangered (CR)
